metadata.name: Pakistan Information Security Framework (PISF) 2026
metadata.description: Baseline information security controls for Pakistani federal and provincial government ministries, divisions and departments, autonomous bodies, corporations, CERTs and designated Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). PISF establishes mandatory baseline controls issued by NTISB and nCERT under the National Cyber Security Policy 2021 and the CERT Rules 2023, structured as a set of essential-control documents.
metadata.source_organization: National Cyber Emergency Response Team (nCERT / PKCERT), Government of Pakistan
metadata.classification_reasoning: PISF is a government-issued mandatory baseline of information security controls (predominantly using 'shall' / 'must') issued by NTISB and nCERT under the National Cyber Security Policy 2021 and CERT Rules 2023, applicable to designated public-sector entities and CIIs, with oversight audits by nCERT/NTISB/sectoral CERTs/Regulator. It is therefore a regulatory compliance framework. NOTE: The framework introduction lists 13 constituent documents, but the supplied PDF contains only 12; document (2) 'Essential Asset and Risk Management Controls' is referenced in the index but its control text is not present in the source, so no controls are numbered under document 2.
metadata.framework_purpose: To establish a mandatory baseline of essential information security controls ensuring consistent protection of information and systems across Pakistani public-sector organizations and CIIs, in compliance with the National Cyber Security Policy 2021 and CERT Rules 2023.
metadata.framework_scope: Applies to all federal and provincial government ministries, divisions and departments, autonomous bodies, corporations, CERTs and designated CIIs (collectively 'organization'), including employees, contractors and third parties, across on-premises, cloud and third-party environments. Scale of implementation varies with organization size.
framework_objectives: Establish foundational governance, policies, roles and oversight for information security
Protect systems, networks, endpoints, data and communications through baseline security controls
Ensure identity, access and privileged-access management across all identities
Protect and preserve the privacy of personal and organizational data
Enable effective incident response, business continuity and disaster recovery
Secure physical facilities, data centres and hosting services
Embed security across the software development lifecycle and the supply chain
Assure compliance through independent audits and continuous improvement
Provide enhanced protection for designated Critical Information Infrastructure (CII)
metadata.target_audience: Federal and provincial government ministries, divisions and departments, autonomous bodies, corporations, CERTs and designated CIIs (and their employees, contractors and third parties).
metadata.regulatory_authority: National Telecommunication & Information Security Board (NTISB) and National Cyber Emergency Response Team (nCERT / PKCERT), Government of Pakistan; sectoral CERTs and relevant sector Regulators as applicable.
metadata.penalty_for_non_compliance: Not specified as monetary penalties within the framework text. Compliance is mandatory and subject to oversight audits by nCERT/NTISB, sectoral CERTs and the relevant Regulator under the National Cyber Security Policy 2021 and CERT Rules 2023.
metadata.adoption_approach: Phased, risk-based implementation across four phases (Phase 1 - Governance; Phase 2 - Asset & Risk Management; Phase 3 - Core Controls incl. system/communication protection, IAM, data protection, incident response, physical security, supply chain and continuous monitoring; Phase 4 - Audit), with Security Training embedded throughout. Compliance is assessed per control using an In-Scope/Out-of-Scope applicability determination (Table 1) and a maturity rating (Table 2: Not Compliant, Partially Compliant, Mostly Compliant, Fully Compliant).

hierarchy_structure.numbering_pattern: Document (e.g., Essential Governance Controls) -> Section (A/B/C...) -> Clause (numbered) -> Sub-clause (a/b/c...). control_id is assigned as {document_number}.{clause_number} using the framework's official 13-document ordering; original_reference preserves the document name, section letter and clause number.

controls.title: Leadership and Commitment by Top Management
controls.description: The Head/Top management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment by ensuring: (a) an IS strategy aligned to laws; (b) a devised, executed and periodically reviewed roadmap; (c) an enabling organizational structure with skilled HR and sufficient funding; and (d) senior-management oversight of IS initiatives.
controls.full_text: Head of the organization or Top management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment with respect to the information security by ensuring the following: (a) An information security strategy shall be formulated. The strategy goals shall be in-line with relevant laws and regulations. (b) A roadmap shall be devised and executed to implement the information security strategy and reviewed periodically according to planned intervals or upon change in relevant laws, regulations and guidelines. (c) An organizational structure shall be established supporting information security governance and operations, ensuring availability of skilled human resources, planning and allocation of sufficient financial resources for effective information security operations. (d) Senior management shall oversee information security initiatives by emphasizing their significance, mandating comprehensive security training, verifying effectiveness, guiding personnel, fostering continuous improvement, and supporting cyber/information security teams in establishing a resilient security posture that aligns with the organization's risk profile and sensitivity levels.

controls.title: Minimum Network Security Management Requirements
controls.description: Network security management shall include at least: physical protection; network segregation; perimeter controls (Firewall, IDS/IPS); secured remote connectivity (VPN, monitoring, auditing, preferably MFA); secure isolated wireless; internet-facing systems segregated from critical systems; logged/monitored network activity; and change/configuration management for network changes.
controls.full_text: The information security requirements for network security management shall include at least the following: a) Physical protection of all network infrastructure and information assets. b) Appropriate segregation of networks across different environments and functions. c) Appropriate perimeter security controls (like Firewall, IDS/IPS, etc. as per the requirements identified by the steering committee of information security). d) Remote connectivity (on strict need basis) secured with appropriate measures, including VPNs, monitoring, auditing, and preferably multi-factor authentication. e) Secure management of wireless networks, isolated from critical internal resources. f) Systems with internet access are logically or physically segregated from critical information systems. g) Network activity is logged and monitored to support incident investigation, security auditing, and compliance requirements. h) Establish and enforce change management and configuration management controls for all network changes and configuration updates.

controls.full_text: Event log and monitoring requirements shall include at least the following: a) Comprehensive event logging of, at a minimum, all critical assets, remote access connections and privileged user accounts. b) Centralized log management and monitoring to aggregate, correlate, and continuously analyze cybersecurity events. c) Retention of critical event logs for a minimum of 12 months for critical assets and for non-critical assets that impact critical assets; and for a minimum of 3 months for all other assets. d) Systems synchronized clocks using NTP (Network Time Protocol). e) Protection of active and archived logs from unauthorized tampering, destruction, or alteration, whether intentional or unintentional, to ensure their integrity and accuracy.

controls.title: Minimum Data Center / Hosting Security Controls
controls.description: Organizations providing hosting or maintaining own data centers/servers shall implement at least: network/perimeter security (NGFW, WAF, IDS/IPS, DDoS, DLP, segmentation, DMZ, secure protocols); server hardening; documented patch/vulnerability management; tested BCP/DRP; continuous monitoring/IR (SIEM, SOAR, SOC); structured cable management; secure logging (≥12 months retention); and secure encrypted backup with offsite/geo-separate storage.
controls.full_text: Organizations that provide hosting services to other entities, or that maintain their own data centers or servers, shall implement and maintain the following minimum security controls: a) Implement network and perimeter security controls, including Next generation firewalls (NGFWs), WAFs, IDS/IPS, DDoS protection, DLP solutions, network segmentation, DMZs, and use of secure communication protocols. b) Implement server hardening practices including limiting unnecessary services, disabling unused ports, enforcement of secure configuration, configuration baseline management and enforcing secure protocols. c) Implement and maintain a documented patch and vulnerability management process to identify, prioritize, remediate, and track vulnerabilities, supported by regular vulnerability assessments and remediation verification. d) Develop, implement, and regularly test Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plans to ensure operational continuity in line with organizational requirements, recovery objectives and service criticality. e) Deploy continuous monitoring and incident response solutions, including SIEM, SOAR, and SOC. f) Implement structured cable management practices, including labelling, separation of power and data cables, and regular inspections to prevent operational and security risks. g) Secure logging and monitoring practices, including retention of critical security event logs for a minimum of 12 months, ensuring integrity, availability, and audit traceability. h) Secure backup and recovery mechanisms, including encryption, access controls, periodic restoration testing, and offsite or geographically separate backup storage.

controls.title: SSDLC Minimum Requirements
controls.description: SSDLC requirements shall include (but not be limited to): security embedded from earliest stages aligned to recognized frameworks; security across all SDLC phases; validation/approval of code before release with post-implementation reviews; role-based secure-coding training; separated dev/test/prod environments; secure repositories; security review/approval of third-party components; approved tooling integrated into CI/CD; comprehensive testing (SAST, DAST, IAST, SCA); and independent/third-party security testing for critical software.
controls.full_text: The requirements for SSDLC shall have but not limited to the following: a) Embed security from the earliest stages of software development and ensure alignment with recognized secure development standards and frameworks. b) Security integrated throughout all phases of the SDLC, including requirements analysis, architecture and design, threat modeling, development, testing, deployment, and maintenance, incorporating risk, compliance and regulatory consideration. c) Security validation and approval of code before release, with post-implementation reviews. d) Appropriate role based training for developers and evaluators in secure coding practices, secure design principles, and emerging threats relevant to the technologies in use. e) Separate development, testing, and production environments with controlled access, change management, and monitoring. f) Maintain secure repositories for source code, build artifacts and configuration items. g) Security review and approval for all commercial, open-source, and third-party components (software libraries, modules, middleware, etc.) before acquisition and integration. h) Adoption of approved tools for code scanning, security testing, dependency management, and version control, integrated into the CI/CD pipeline. i) Comprehensive testing through expert code reviews and manual/automated assessments of all software and applications (e.g., SAST, DAST, IAST, SCA), appropriate to the application's risk and criticality. j) Ensure that independent or third-party security testing is performed for critical software and applications as part of the secure development and acquisition lifecycle.
